claims.text: RequestLoggingMiddleware.InvokeAsync (stage-1:11-23) awaits next(context) and only afterwards calls LogInformation with the template "{Method} {Path} responded {StatusCode} in {ElapsedMs}ms"; if next throws, the log call is not reached.

At stage-1 ExceptionHandlingMiddleware is registered before RequestLoggingMiddleware in Program.cs, catches exceptions from later middleware and logs them (LogWarning/LogError) before writing the response.

docker-compose.yml@stage-1:82-88: service api, image donhang-api:stage-1, container_name donhang-api, hostname api; the api service (to line 99) has no logging setting, and no service in the stage-1 lab reads container output.
Docker keeps what a container writes to stdout/stderr, and docker compose logs <service> prints it; --since accepts a relative duration such as 5m or 2m.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker compose logs (--since); Docker docs: View container logs

claims.text: With the default console formatter, a LogInformation event from RequestLoggingMiddleware appears as 'info: DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware[0]' followed by an indented line like 'GET /api/v1/products responded 200 in 4ms'.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Logging, console formatters (simple); backend.l1.structured-logging Try it (verified at stage-1)

claims.text: docker compose logs api --since 5m | grep -c "responded 5" counts the lines of the last five minutes that contain 'responded 5' (grep -c prints the number of lines containing the text), so it matches responded 500, 503 alike.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker compose logs; GNU grep manual (-c)

claims.text: Log line = one event with details; metric = one number measured repeatedly; with a count held as a metric, failures in the last 5 minutes = value now minus value 5 minutes ago, unless the API restarted in between (a count kept by the process starts again from zero).
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Concepts / Data model (definition level)

claims.text: Log volume grows with every request; a metric split by status code keeps one number per status code seen, so its size depends on how many distinct things it counts, not on traffic.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Data model; Prometheus docs: Naming / label cardinality (principle level)

claims.text: When the api container is stopped, Caddy's reverse_proxy api:8080 cannot reach an upstream and answers the request itself with an error status (a 5xx, such as 502); the API writes nothing about those requests.
claims.source_hint: Caddy docs: reverse_proxy (upstream errors -> 502); examples/don-hang @ stage-1: Caddyfile handle /api/v1/*; live run 2026-09-29: 502, no api log line

claims.text:
Try it: after docker compose stop api, curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" (sends GET, prints only the status code) to localhost:8080/api/v1/products prints an error status from Caddy (a 5xx such as 502); docker compose logs api --since 2m has no line about those requests.
claims.source_hint: run on the stage-1 lab (Compose v2.33); Docker docs: docker compose stop/start/logs; live run 2026-09-29: 502, no api log line

claims.text: Monitoring is continuous collection by programs, not a person watching a screen; the value is that numbers exist for periods nobody watched.
A metric keeps a number and drops per-event details; logs keep the details, so a rise in a 5xx count still needs log lines to find which path failed.
Each request that returns normally adds two lines to the container output: the Simple console formatter prints one event as a header line and an indented message line.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: console log formatter (Simple)
